record.original_question: Does every graph admit an embedding in Euclidean 3-space whose edges are straight-line segments of integer lengths; if not, what is the minimum dimension d needed for each graph?

evidence.quote: Question 8.2 Does every graph have an embedding in 3-space so that the edges are line segments of integer lengths? If the answer to either of the preceding two questions is no, then what can be said about the minimum number d such that the graph has an integer-length representation in Euclidean d-space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A straight-line embedding of a (finite, simple) graph $G=(V,E)$ in Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$ is an injective map $f:V\to\mathbb{R}^d$ such that, when each edge $uv\in E$ is drawn as the closed straight-line segment from $f(u)$ to $f(v)$, distinct edges intersect only at common endpoints. Such an embedding is said to have integer edge lengths if for every edge $uv\in E$ the Euclidean distance $\|f(u)-f(v)\|$ is a positive integer.

(a) Does every finite simple graph $G$ admit a straight-line embedding in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with integer edge lengths?

(b) If the answer to (a) is negative, determine, for each finite simple graph $G$, the minimum integer $d=d(G)$ such that $G$ admits a straight-line embedding in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with integer edge lengths, and characterize $d(G)$ in terms of graph-theoretic parameters of $G$.
artifact.status_search_result: The closely related Harborth conjecture (whether every planar graph admits a straight-line drawing in the plane with integer edge lengths) remains open. The higher-dimensional analogue, asking whether every graph admits an integer-length straight-line embedding in $\mathbb{R}^3$ (and otherwise determining the minimum dimension required), does not appear to have a known resolution in the literature.

status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of straight-line embeddings of graphs in Euclidean spaces; the general integer-length version is not noted as resolved.
status_evidence.claim: No known resolution of the integer-length 3-space embedding problem is recorded.

status_evidence.title: Embedding graphs in Euclidean space (arXiv 1802.03092)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on Euclidean embeddings of graphs; integer-length variants in 3-space are still investigated.
status_evidence.claim: Integer-length embedding questions in higher dimensions remain active research.
